definition: Ignominious means deeply shameful and humiliating.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ignominious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ignominious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The mascot's debut was ignominious: he tripped on the flag, slid helmet-first into the tuba section, and was retired by halftime.
Awkward stops far short of ignominious — an awkward stumble is forgotten by morning.
Embarrassing stops short of ignominious — an embarrassing moment makes you blush, while an ignominious one stains your public name.

Disgraceful condemns the conduct itself — the act was shameful and wrong, whoever saw it happen. Ignominious shifts the weight onto the aftermath: the public shame that clings to a person afterward. Cheating is disgraceful the moment it happens; being stripped of the trophy on stage is ignominious.

Humiliating describes what an experience does to you: it wounds personal pride, and it can do that with no one else watching. Ignominious adds a public stage and a stain that lasts — ignominious defeat makes the papers. You can be humiliated privately; ignominy needs witnesses.

Ignominious is for public disgrace with staying power — routs, scandals, downfall.
A private fumble is merely 'embarrassing'; save ignominious for shame that makes the papers and follows the name around afterward.
